name: SelvedgeBlur
description: A progressive blur along one edge of a scrolling area or image: stacked layers of backdrop blur that fade from sharp to blurred, so content softens as it nears the edge. Pure decoration: it ignores the pointer and is hidden from assistive technology.

position.description: Which edge of the parent is blurred. start and end follow the reading direction.

strength.description: Blur radius in px at the very edge.

size.description: How far the blur reaches in from the edge, any CSS length.

layers.description: Number of stacked blur layers. More layers give a smoother fade.

requirements: Decoration only: aria-hidden, never focusable, and pointer-events none so the content below stays clickable and selectable
It does not move, so there is nothing to pause; the blur is the same for visitors who prefer reduced motion
It only softens what is under it: do not put content the reader needs to read inside the blurred zone
In forced-colors (high contrast) mode the blur is removed, so text is never obscured
Place it inside a positioned parent (position: relative), above the content in stacking order

use_when: The edge of a scrolling list or feed that continues off screen
The bottom of a card with an image behind text
avoid_when: Over text that must stay readable
Where backdrop-filter is not wanted for performance reasons on long pages
anti_patterns: Covering interactive controls, which become hard to see
Using a large strength with a tiny size, which looks like a hard band
